angle: exp as the limit of discrete compounding: (1+x/n)^n is literally Euler's method for y'=y, its binomial expansion bridges term-by-term to the power series, its limit is finite (the ceiling e), and the integer power law (1+h)^{m+k}=(1+h)^m(1+h)^k gives exp(x+y)=exp(x)exp(y) exactly before any limit is taken

libraries.name: p5.js
libraries.role: two bespoke instance-mode canvases: (a) the ledger staircase — n multiplicative risers over [0,x] with the smooth e^t curve behind, per-slice pointer picking linked to the HTML ledger table, a labelled riser showing increment = amount x dt, a shortfall bracket at t=x, and a step-by-step 'run the ledger' animation; (b) the additivity movie — two coloured staircase segments plus a dashed rescaled copy of segment 1 magnified by A=exp(x) that lands exactly on segment 2

libraries.name: Chart.js
libraries.role: the three statistical plots: balance-vs-n on a logarithmic x-axis flattening under a dashed asymptote at e (the ceiling); grouped/overlaid bars of the binomial term C(n,k)(x/n)^k against its limit x^k/k! on a log y-axis; and a log-log error-vs-work chart contrasting compounding's e/(2n) decay with the series' 1/(N+1)!

libraries.name: big.js
libraries.role: 70-decimal-digit arithmetic for every headline value: (1+x/n)^n via binary exponentiation with explicit rounding after each multiply, e via the power series, and the ground truth against which the IEEE-double failure at n=10^16 is exhibited

libraries.name: KaTeX
libraries.role: all mathematical notation — static statements via a data-tex/data-tex-d attribute scanner, plus generated expressions rebuilt on every slider move (the bracket product B_k(n), the exponent identity, the chain of inequalities)

building_blocks: vertical-fold section scaffold: numbered <section> beats separated by rules, each with eyebrow/h2/sub, and a sticky top nav of anchor pills

ledger-paper theme tokens: warm manila background with repeating accounting rule lines, cream cards, and a three-colour semantic scheme (copper = discrete/finite-n, green = continuous/limit, red = the ceiling and the error)
KaTeX attribute scanner: renderStaticTeX() sweeping [data-tex] inline and [data-tex-d] display, idempotent via a data-done guard, plus a tex(el, src, display) helper for regenerated math

high-precision power helper: bpow(base, exp) binary exponentiation over big.js with rounding to a fixed dp after every multiply (exact multiplication would double the digit count each squaring), using modulo rather than bitwise so exponents above 2^31 survive

exact-rational value formatter: (n+1)^n / n^n computed with native BigInt integer powers and long-divided to d decimal places, giving a genuinely exact decimal string with no floating point in the path
provenance tag component: inline pills (exact / 70 dp / 64-bit) attached to every displayed number so the reader knows which arithmetic produced it
step-ledger data structure: buildLedger(x, n) emitting {k, t, start, interest, end} rows where interest = start * h, so the recursion and the table are the same object
head/tail table renderer: shows the first 7 and last 3 rows with an elided '... N more periods ...' band once n exceeds a threshold, keeping a 8760-row ledger readable

linked canvas-table hover: pointer position inside the p5 canvas maps to a slice index which highlights the ledger row, and row mouseenter drives the canvas highlight back, arbitrated by a ledgerHover flag
stride-decimated polyline: staircase drawing that walks corner points with a stride once risers fall below a pixel, keeping n = 8760 at 60 fps without faking the geometry
p5 instance-mode canvas host: sketch factory parented to a div, pixelDensity clamp, and windowResized re-measuring the container
index-snapped slider: range input over an array of meaningful values (1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12, 26, 52, 365, 8760) with a human label (annually / monthly / hourly) instead of a raw number
log-ramp slider: range index mapped through a power law so one control reaches n = 1 to 2000 with useful resolution at both ends
decade-only gridline callback for Chart.js logarithmic axes (log scales otherwise paint a minor gridline at every tick and hatch the plot)
superscript-digit formatter for scientific notation in plain-text tick labels and table cells
chip ladder: a product written as a row of per-factor chips with semantic classes (approaching one / exactly zero / result)
three-column inequality bars: nested absolute-positioned CSS bars showing term <= 1/k! <= 1/2^(k-1) per row with running totals beneath
tab-panel group with a resize hook, so a Chart.js canvas built inside a display:none panel is re-laid-out the first time it is revealed
honesty callout component: bordered, tinted note blocks in three severities used to surface asserted-not-proved steps, numerical failure modes and method cost
computations: the compounding recursion y_{k+1} = y_k (1 + x/n) evaluated period by period, with the per-period interest shown as amount x (x/n) to expose it as (rate)(amount)(dt)
(1 + x/n)^n at 70 decimal digits via big.js binary exponentiation with per-multiply rounding, for n from 1 to 10^17
exact rational (n+1)^n / n^n via native BigInt integer powers, long-divided to 12 places, for every table row with n <= 400 (n = 1, 2, 3, 4, 10, 12, 52, 100, 365)
e = sum 1/k! computed to 70 digits with big.js, used as the reference for every error figure
e^x to 70 digits by the same series, compared against the ledger total at the user's x
the binomial bracket B_k(n) = prod_{j=0}^{k-1} (1 - j/n), factor by factor, including its collapse to exactly 0 once k > n
the binomial term C(n,k)(x/n)^k rewritten as (x^k/k!) * B_k(n), summed over k to reproduce (1+x/n)^n
the first-order error prediction e/(2n) tabulated beside the measured error e - (1+1/n)^n
marginal gain per table row and each row's share of the total prize e - 2 = 0.71828 (monthly 85.3%, daily 99.48%)
the boundedness chain: B_k(n)/k! <= 1/k! <= 1/2^(k-1) per term, with all three running totals converging to (1+1/n)^n, e and 3
the exact discrete additivity check (1+h)^m (1+h)^k - (1+h)^{m+k} at 70 digits, reported as identically zero
the negative-x failure table: 1 + x/n and (1+x/n)^n for x = -5 across n = 1..10000, classified by sign of the factor, against e^-5
IEEE double vs 70-digit (1+1/n)^n for n = 10^3 .. 10^17, exhibiting the collapse to exactly 1.0
cost comparison: smallest N with |e - sum_{k<=N} 1/k!| < 0.5e-10 (N = 13) against the n needed for the same accuracy by compounding (n ~ 2.7e10)
interactions: n slider (index-snapped: annually, semi-annually, every 4 months, quarterly, bi-monthly, monthly, fortnightly, weekly, daily, hourly) redraws the staircase, rebuilds the ledger table, and updates the slice length, growth factor, 70-digit total and shortfall
term slider x in [0.25, 3] rescales the whole section-1 scene and its target e^x
'Run the ledger' button animates the staircase period by period, sweeping the highlighted riser and its (amount x dt) label
toggle for the smooth e^x curve and the shortfall bracket
hovering the staircase canvas selects a slice and highlights the corresponding ledger row; hovering a ledger row highlights the riser on the canvas (bidirectional)
binomial n slider (log ramp, n = 1..2000) raises the copper term bars toward the green limit bars and drives the bracket chips toward 1
binomial x slider rescales both the actual and limit term bars
k slider selects which term to dissect, rewriting the KaTeX bracket product, the per-factor chip ladder, and the actual/limit/percentage statistics
the same n slider live-updates section 4's three-column inequality bars and their running totals
two month-count sliders (x and y, 1..24) in the additivity section rebuild the two-segment growth movie and the four-way numerical check A, B, A*B, (1+h)^{m+k}
'Overlay the rescaled copy' toggle shows or hides the dashed magnified copy of the first y months, which is the functional equation made visible
three-way tab switch across the honesty panels (negative time / floating point / method cost), resizing the error chart on first reveal
Chart.js tooltips on the ceiling curve reporting the balance to nine places and the shortfall in scientific notation
assets: katex.min.css (font src paths left at the default relative fonts/ directory)
katex .woff2 fonts (all 20 files, vendored under lib/katex/fonts/)
gotchas: big.js multiplication is exact, so naive binary exponentiation doubles the digit count on every squaring and grinds to a halt; the fix is to round to a fixed working precision (70 dp) after each multiply, which costs about 20 roundings of 1e-70 each - invisible against the 15 digits displayed

bpow originally used `n & 1` for the parity test; JavaScript bitwise operators coerce to int32, which silently corrupts every exponent above 2^31 - the floating-point panel goes to n = 10^17, so parity must use `n % 2`

a stray `*/` left behind while editing a block comment silently killed the entire IIFE with 'Uncaught SyntaxError: Unexpected token *' and the page rendered as bare unstyled HTML with no other symptom; catching it required running headless Chrome with --enable-logging=stderr --v=1 and grepping for CONSOLE, since --dump-dom alone reports nothing

Chart.js logarithmic axes draw a gridline at every minor tick, hatching the plot; a grid color callback that returns a transparent colour for non-decade ticks fixes it, and tick labels need autoSkip:false or the callback's chosen decades get skipped away
a Chart.js canvas built inside a display:none tab panel initialises at zero size; call chart.resize() when the panel is first revealed
CSS text-transform:uppercase on label styling mangles inline mathematics (x^k/k! became X^K/K!, 1+x/n became 1+X/N); math-bearing labels must opt out
monospace ledger tables with white-space:nowrap overflow narrow grid columns and clip silently - either shorten headers and padding or promote the table to its own full-width row
p5.js instance mode is required to host two independent sketches and to avoid it hijacking the global namespace or auto-creating a stray canvas
drawing 8760 risers plus a matching fill polygon every frame stalls the draw loop; walking the corner points with a stride once risers are sub-pixel keeps it honest and fast
KaTeX refuses to render in quirks mode, so the page must open with a real <!DOCTYPE html>
KaTeX's stylesheet references fonts by the relative path fonts/*.woff2, so the fonts directory must be vendored as a sibling of katex.min.css or every glyph silently falls back

the binomial bracket self-truncates: B_k(n) contains the factor (1 - n/n) = 0 once k > n, which is mathematically correct but produces zeros that a logarithmic bar axis cannot plot - worth stating in the UI rather than clamping
